lines.raw: Lesson 5: Government & Program Words.
lines.say: Lesson 5: Government and Program Words.

lines.raw: Medicare, Medicaid, CHIP, the ACA and CMS: the public side of US healthcare.
lines.say: Medicare, Medicaid, CHIP, the A C A and C M S: the public side of U S healthcare.

lines.raw: In this lesson you will:
lines.say: In this lesson you will:

lines.raw: Tell Medicare, Medicaid and CHIP apart.
lines.say: Tell Medicare, Medicaid and CHIP apart.

lines.raw: Name the four parts of Medicare and explain Medicare Advantage.
lines.say: Name the four parts of Medicare and explain Medicare Advantage.

lines.raw: Explain what the ACA and the marketplace are.
lines.say: Explain what the A C A and the marketplace are.

lines.raw: Know what CMS does, and where the privacy words (HIPAA, PHI) are taught.
lines.say: Know what C M S does, and where the privacy words (HIPAA, P H I) are taught.

lines.raw: Where do Americans get coverage?
lines.say: Where do Americans get coverage?

lines.raw: Emily gets her coverage from her **employer**, like most working-age Americans.
lines.say: Emily gets her coverage from her employer, like most working-age Americans.

lines.raw: But the government also runs huge health programs, for older people, for people with low income, and for children.
lines.say: But the government also runs huge health programs, for older people, for people with low income, and for children.

lines.raw: These words come up all the time, even if you only work with commercial (employer) data.
lines.say: These words come up all the time, even if you only work with commercial (employer) data.

lines.raw: The main sources of US coverage.
lines.say: The main sources of U S coverage.

lines.raw: **Commercial (employer)**. Who it covers: Workers and their families. Who pays: Employer and worker share the premium. Our example: Emily, Daniel and Lily.
lines.say: Commercial (employer). Who it covers: Workers and their families. Who pays: Employer and worker share the premium. Our example: Emily, Daniel and Lily.

lines.raw: **Individual / marketplace**. Who it covers: People who buy their own plan. Who pays: The person, often with a government subsidy. Our example: Daniel could have used this after losing his job.
lines.say: Individual or marketplace. Who it covers: People who buy their own plan. Who pays: The person, often with a government subsidy. Our example: Daniel could have used this after losing his job.

lines.raw: **Medicare**. Who it covers: People **65 and older**, and some younger people with disabilities or kidney failure. Who pays: Federal government, plus member premiums. Our example: Robert, Emily's father.
lines.say: Medicare. Who it covers: People 65 and older, and some younger people with disabilities or kidney failure. Who pays: Federal government, plus member premiums. Our example: Robert, Emily's father.

lines.raw: **Medicaid**. Who it covers: People with **low income** (rules vary by state). Who pays: Federal and state governments together. Our example: None of our characters.
lines.say: Medicaid. Who it covers: People with low income (rules vary by state). Who pays: Federal and state governments together. Our example: None of our characters.

lines.raw: **CHIP**. Who it covers: **Children** in families that earn too much for Medicaid but cannot afford private cover. Who pays: Federal and state governments. Our example: None of our characters.
lines.say: CHIP. Who it covers: Children in families that earn too much for Medicaid but cannot afford private cover. Who pays: Federal and state governments. Our example: None of our characters.

lines.raw: An easy way to remember.
lines.say: An easy way to remember.

lines.raw: Medi**care** is for the elderly, people we **care** for.
lines.say: Medicare is for the elderly, people we care for.

lines.raw: Medic**aid** is **aid** for people with low income.
lines.say: Medicaid is aid for people with low income.

lines.raw: Meet Robert: our Medicare member.
lines.say: Meet Robert: our Medicare member.

lines.raw: In the US: Robert Carter, Houston, Texas.
lines.say: In the U S: Robert Carter, Houston, Texas.

lines.raw: **Robert** is Emily's father, born **2 May 1957**, a retired school teacher in Houston.
lines.say: Robert is Emily's father, born 2 May 1957, a retired school teacher in Houston.

lines.raw: He turned 65 in May 2022 and joined **Medicare**.
lines.say: He turned 65 in May 2022 and joined Medicare.

lines.raw: He has **type 2 diabetes** and **high blood pressure**.
lines.say: He has type 2 diabetes and high blood pressure.

lines.raw: From May 2022 to the end of 2023, Robert had **Original Medicare** (Parts A and B) plus a separate **Part D** drug plan from a private company.
lines.say: From May 2022 to the end of 2023, Robert had Original Medicare (Parts A and B) plus a separate Part D drug plan from a private company.

lines.raw: Since **1 January 2024** he has a **Medicare Advantage** plan with drug coverage: **Gulf Coast Advantage (HMO)** from **Gulf Coast Health Plan** (made up), member ID `GC5001`.
lines.say: Since 1 January 2024 he has a Medicare Advantage plan with drug coverage: Gulf Coast Advantage (H M O) from Gulf Coast Health Plan (made up), member I D G C 5 0 0 1.

lines.raw: His primary care doctor is **Dr. Nguyen** at Bayou Family Medicine (made up).
lines.say: His primary care doctor is Doctor Nguyen at Bayou Family Medicine (made up).

lines.raw: His claims go to his Medicare Advantage plan, not to Emily's employer plan.
lines.say: His claims go to his Medicare Advantage plan, not to Emily's employer plan.

lines.raw: He still pays the monthly Part B premium.
lines.say: He still pays the monthly Part B premium.

lines.raw: Part A (Hospital insurance).
lines.say: Part A (Hospital insurance).

lines.raw: Inpatient hospital stays, skilled nursing facility care, hospice and some home health.
lines.say: Inpatient hospital stays, skilled nursing facility care, hospice and some home health.

lines.raw: Most people pay **no premium** for Part A because they paid Medicare taxes while working.
lines.say: Most people pay no premium for Part A because they paid Medicare taxes while working.

lines.raw: Part B (Medical insurance).
lines.say: Part B (Medical insurance).

lines.raw: Doctor visits, outpatient care, lab tests, preventive care and medical equipment.
lines.say: Doctor visits, outpatient care, lab tests, preventive care and medical equipment.

lines.raw: Has a **monthly premium** (the standard amount in 2025 is $185.00).
lines.say: Has a monthly premium (the standard amount in 2025 is 185 dollars).

lines.raw: Part C (Medicare Advantage, MA).
lines.say: Part C (Medicare Advantage, M A).

lines.raw: A **private health plan approved by Medicare** that replaces Parts A and B (and usually includes D).
lines.say: A private health plan approved by Medicare that replaces Parts A and B (and usually includes D).

lines.raw: Medicare pays the plan a fixed monthly amount per member.
lines.say: Medicare pays the plan a fixed monthly amount per member.

lines.raw: Roughly **half** of people with Medicare now choose MA.
lines.say: Roughly half of people with Medicare now choose M A.

lines.raw: Part D (Prescription drugs).
lines.say: Part D (Prescription drugs).

lines.raw: Drug coverage sold by **private companies** approved by Medicare, either as a standalone plan (Robert's choice in 2022 and 2023) or inside a Medicare Advantage plan (Robert's choice since 2024).
lines.say: Drug coverage sold by private companies approved by Medicare, either as a standalone plan (Robert's choice in 2022 and 2023) or inside a Medicare Advantage plan (Robert's choice since 2024).

lines.raw: Original Medicare (Fee-for-Service Medicare).
lines.say: Original Medicare (Fee-for-Service Medicare).

lines.raw: Parts A and B run **directly by the government**.
lines.say: Parts A and B run directly by the government.

lines.raw: While Robert had it (2022 to 2023), he could see almost any doctor in the US who accepts Medicare.
lines.say: While Robert had it (2022 to 2023), he could see almost any doctor in the U S who accepts Medicare.

lines.raw: Medigap (Medicare Supplement).
lines.say: Medigap (Medicare Supplement).

lines.raw: Extra private insurance that helps pay the costs Original Medicare leaves to the member, such as coinsurance.
lines.say: Extra private insurance that helps pay the costs Original Medicare leaves to the member, such as coinsurance.

lines.raw: Dual eligible ("duals").
lines.say: Dual eligible ("duals").

lines.raw: A person who has **both Medicare and Medicaid**, usually older people with low income.
lines.say: A person who has both Medicare and Medicaid, usually older people with low income.

lines.raw: Beneficiary.
lines.say: Beneficiary.

lines.raw: The usual word for a person covered by Medicare or Medicaid, the same as a member in a commercial plan.
lines.say: The usual word for a person covered by Medicare or Medicaid, the same as a member in a commercial plan.

lines.raw: Original Medicare vs Medicare Advantage.
lines.say: Original Medicare versus Medicare Advantage.

lines.raw: Think of a government canteen and a private caterer.
lines.say: Think of a government canteen and a private caterer.

lines.raw: With **Original Medicare**, Robert eats at the government canteen and the government pays for each plate he eats (fee for service).
lines.say: With Original Medicare, Robert eats at the government canteen and the government pays for each plate he eats (fee for service).

lines.raw: With **Medicare Advantage**, the government gives a private caterer a fixed amount each month to feed Robert, and the caterer decides the menu, often adding extras like dental or vision.
lines.say: With Medicare Advantage, the government gives a private caterer a fixed amount each month to feed Robert, and the caterer decides the menu, often adding extras like dental or vision.

lines.raw: Nepal also has a government health insurance program, run by the **Health Insurance Board**, where families pay a yearly contribution for cover at listed health facilities.
lines.say: Nepal also has a government health insurance program, run by the Health Insurance Board, where families pay a yearly contribution for cover at listed health facilities.

lines.raw: Like Medicaid, it is a **public** program, and the government supports some groups, such as people with very low income.
lines.say: Like Medicaid, it is a public program, and the government supports some groups, such as people with very low income.

lines.raw: Sita's SSF is different: it is linked to her **job** and her contributions, which makes it closer in spirit to US **employer** coverage plus a government-style fund.
lines.say: Sita's S S F is different: it is linked to her job and her contributions, which makes it closer in spirit to U S employer coverage plus a government-style fund.

lines.raw: About Nepal programs.
lines.say: About Nepal programs.

lines.raw: Health Insurance Board and SSF rules, contributions and limits change over time.
lines.say: Health Insurance Board and S S F rules, contributions and limits change over time.

lines.raw: This lesson only compares the broad ideas.
lines.say: This lesson only compares the broad ideas.

lines.raw: Check official sources for current details.
lines.say: Check official sources for current details.

lines.raw: The law and the agency.
lines.say: The law and the agency.

lines.raw: ACA (Affordable Care Act, "Obamacare").
lines.say: A C A (Affordable Care Act, "Obamacare").

lines.raw: A major US law passed in **2010**.
lines.say: A major U S law passed in 2010.

lines.raw: It created the **marketplaces**, stopped insurers refusing people for **pre-existing conditions**, let children stay on a parent's plan **until age 26**, and let states **expand Medicaid**.
lines.say: It created the marketplaces, stopped insurers refusing people for pre-existing conditions, let children stay on a parent's plan until age 26, and let states expand Medicaid.

lines.raw: Marketplace (exchange).
lines.say: Marketplace (exchange).

lines.raw: A government-run website where people **buy their own plan**, often with **subsidies** (tax credits) based on income.
lines.say: A government-run website where people buy their own plan, often with subsidies (tax credits) based on income.

lines.raw: The federal one is HealthCare.gov; some states run their own.
lines.say: The federal one is HealthCare.gov; some states run their own.

lines.raw: Metal tiers.
lines.say: Metal tiers.

lines.raw: Marketplace plans are labelled **Bronze, Silver, Gold, Platinum**.
lines.say: Marketplace plans are labelled Bronze, Silver, Gold, Platinum.

lines.raw: Bronze has the lowest premium but the highest cost sharing; Platinum is the reverse.
lines.say: Bronze has the lowest premium but the highest cost sharing; Platinum is the reverse.

lines.raw: CMS (Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services).
lines.say: C M S (Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services).

lines.raw: The **federal agency** that runs Medicare, oversees Medicaid and CHIP with the states, and runs the federal marketplace.
lines.say: The federal agency that runs Medicare, oversees Medicaid and CHIP with the states, and runs the federal marketplace.

lines.raw: It sets many of the rules and code standards the whole industry follows.
lines.say: It sets many of the rules and code standards the whole industry follows.

lines.raw: COBRA.
lines.say: COBRA.

lines.raw: A law that lets people **keep their employer plan for a while** after losing their job, usually by paying the full premium themselves.
lines.say: A law that lets people keep their employer plan for a while after losing their job, usually by paying the full premium themselves.

lines.raw: Daniel could have used COBRA, but joining Emily's plan was cheaper.
lines.say: Daniel could have used COBRA, but joining Emily's plan was cheaper.

lines.raw: Why Lily is on Emily's plan, not on CHIP.
lines.say: Why Lily is on Emily's plan, not on CHIP.

lines.raw: CHIP is for children whose families cannot afford private coverage.
lines.say: CHIP is for children whose families cannot afford private coverage.

lines.raw: Lily is already covered as a **dependent** on Emily's employer plan, and under the ACA she can stay on it until she turns **26**.
lines.say: Lily is already covered as a dependent on Emily's employer plan, and under the A C A she can stay on it until she turns 26.

lines.raw: Privacy words: HIPAA and PHI.
lines.say: Privacy words: HIPAA and P H I.

lines.raw: One law every data worker meets.
lines.say: One law every data worker meets.

lines.raw: **HIPAA** is the US law that protects **PHI** (Protected Health Information: health data that can identify a person, such as Emily's name and member ID `M1001` next to her diagnosis).
lines.say: HIPAA is the U S law that protects P H I (Protected Health Information: health data that can identify a person, such as Emily's name and member I D M 1 0 0 1 next to her diagnosis).

lines.raw: The words around it, such as covered entity, business associate, minimum necessary and de-identified data, are taught in the HIPAA course.
lines.say: The words around it, such as covered entity, business associate, minimum necessary and de-identified data, are taught in the HIPAA course.

lines.raw: Key takeaways.
lines.say: Key takeaways.

lines.raw: **Medicare** = 65+ (and some disabled people).
lines.say: Medicare = 65+ (and some disabled people).

lines.raw: **Medicaid** = low income, run with states.
lines.say: Medicaid = low income, run with states.

lines.raw: **CHIP** = children.
lines.say: CHIP = children.

lines.raw: Medicare parts: **A** hospital, **B** medical, **C** Medicare Advantage (private plans), **D** drugs.
lines.say: Medicare parts: A hospital, B medical, C Medicare Advantage (private plans), D drugs.

lines.raw: The **ACA** (2010) created the **marketplaces** and many consumer protections.
lines.say: The A C A (2010) created the marketplaces and many consumer protections.

lines.raw: **CMS** is the federal agency that runs Medicare and oversees Medicaid.
lines.say: C M S is the federal agency that runs Medicare and oversees Medicaid.

lines.raw: **HIPAA** protects **PHI**, health data that can identify a person; the HIPAA course teaches the details.
lines.say: HIPAA protects P H I, health data that can identify a person; the HIPAA course teaches the details.
